Q: bullmq deduplicate job while keeping the last one in the queue A:

If I understand correctly, the user is updating the config and re-deploying the site. If that's the case, you should:

  1. Save the new config to the DB
  2. Pass the config into the job
  3. If there are still race conditions, you can query the site's config from the DB in the job itself.

Q: Share TypeORM entities and services across multiple NestJS apps via a private library A:

Being that the CatsModule is in an entirely different library, it is referring to a completely separate instance of the TypeORMModule. In it's context, the TypeORMModule.forRootAsync() method has not been called, and therefore the module has not been registered.

You can export the @Entity() classes from the shared library, but not the TypeOrmModule.forFeature()s.

Q: Should I use separate processes or worker threads with BullMQ for asynchronous tasks in NestJS? A:

Asynchronous would be anything that involves I/O. Common examples are network requests (HTTP, Database requests), and file system operations.

Synchronous tasks would be CPU operations like arithmetic, string manipulation, looping through arrays, managing data structures and performing algorithms.

Separating your worker processor from your web processor for synchronous tasks is highly recommended. That way the web server can cotinue to run smoothly without being bogged down by the CPU-intensive tasks.

Separating your worker processor from your web processor could also be beneficial to provide looser coupling between the two. This will ensure that your web processor has as much resources as it can get, which will affect response time as you scale. It also provides a safety net. If something causes the worker processor to crash, the web processor can continue running smoothly. Lastly, it also provides more control. If you want to shut off background processing for some time without affecting the web server, you can do so easily.

Q: LD_LIBRARY_PATH for gtest_discover_tests (in QtCreator?) A:

I hit this same problem.

The solution: gtest_discover_tests() looks for a TEST_LAUNCHER property on the test executable. You can use cmake -E env as the launcher, setting LD_LIBRARY_PATH (and any other environment variables your test might need to run).

Note that TEST_LAUNCHER is treated as an argument list; so, the arguments should be semi-colon-separated rather than space-separated.

Q: How to safely handle failed BullMQ jobs and Redis memory limits without data loss? A:

One of the amazing features of BullMQ is how it handles failed jobs.

Any failed job will be moved to the "failed" queue.

You can programatically access this queue, or you can use BullBoard, an open-source GUI that you can plug into your web application. It allows you to read logs, retry failed jobs, pause and resume queues and more.

As for your Redis setup, if you're concerned about data loss, I'd recommend setting your Redis instance to write to an AOF (append-only file). You can read more about data persistence in Redis here.

Q: How to detect if an ellipse intersects(collides with) a circle A:

If you're not super fussy about it being perfectly accurate you can just pretend the circle is a point and thicken the oval for a faster to compute solution (I think)

Gets you an equation like:

( relative_x/(rad_x+rad_circ) )^2 + ( relative_y/(rad_y+rad_circ) )^2 < 1

relative_x/y refers to relative distance of centres, rad_x/y refer to ovals radius in each axis

if the oval is rotated the relative x & y coordinates can be transformed in reverse (google some other post)

From my limited checking it works most accuratley when the circle is reasonably smaller than the oval, I have not tested it for extreme ovals e.g width:height = 10:1
